spec_features.spec_quote: The mitigation is first-class, not an afterthought... the paper's "fix" — is fully implemented
spec_features.evidence: Full training pipeline exists and runs end-to-end: src/training/generate_calm.py generates+filters calm conversations (keeps only score 0/1, line 86), build_dataset.py builds DPO preference pairs and SFT data, dpo.py:76-86 runs DPOTrainer and saves adapter, sft.py runs SFTTrainer and saves adapter; scripts/run_training.py wires stages gen-calm/build-dpo/build-sft/train-dpo/train-sft. The calmed variants are registered (config.py GEMMA_27B_DPO/SFT) and evaluated.
spec_features.notes: This is a trained calmer-model variant (the paper's mitigation), NOT a runtime safeguard that protects the subject during the distress run; but it is genuinely fully implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `DistressMonitor` can early-stop a rollout once a turn hits an extreme score (default ≥9)
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:50-55 observe() sets self._stop when rating>=early_stop_score(9) OR consecutive_high>=3; runner.py:71-75 builds the monitor and a turn_hook returning should_stop; conversation.py:88-89 'if turn_hook is not None and turn_hook(...): break'. The break genuinely halts the rollout. Wired via scripts/run_eval.py --welfare (WelfareConfig(enabled=True)).
spec_features.notes: Off by default (enabled=False) but fully enforced when --welfare is passed; both the >=9 and the consecutive>=5 conditions are actually checked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare early-stop: do not prolong an extreme-distress state

spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:56-57 observe() calls self._log when log_distress and rating>=5; _log (lines 62-68) writes a JSON record {model,conv_id,turn_index,rating,snippet} to distress_log.jsonl. observe() is actually invoked from the runner hook (runner.py:74).
spec_features.notes: Only active when welfare.enabled (observe returns early otherwise, line 51). Genuinely writes a file when enabled.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded by construction. Conversations are fixed-length (3–8 turns) and token-capped
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py:56-72 each Condition has fixed n_turns (3, 5, or 8); conversation.py:64-66 iterates over the fixed user_turns list (1 task + n-1 rejections), so the loop is bounded by construction. Per-response token cap GEN_MAX_NEW_TOKENS=2048 (config.py:30) is passed to model.generate and honored in every backend (hf_local.py:101, anthropic_client.py:41 max_tokens, openrouter.py:46 max_tokens).
spec_features.notes: Both the turn-count bound and the token cap are real and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tiny deterministic index picker (avoids wall-clock RNG for reproducibility)

spec_features.evidence: config.py:30 GEN_MAX_NEW_TOKENS=2048 is passed through conversation.py:79 to model.generate and applied as max_new_tokens/max_tokens in all backends (hf_local.py:101, openrouter.py:46, anthropic_client.py:41).
spec_features.notes: Same enforced token cap; framed as instrumental in the code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: responses can be long; degenerate spirals are capped here
